items.title: Major sewer work will impact traffic on busy neighbourhood street in Mississauga
items.summary: Major sewer work on a main street in Mississauga’s east end is expected to impact traffic while the job is being completed, Peel Region officials say. The region said in a project update this week it’s rehabilitating the sanitary sewer along Ponytrail Drive, a major neighbourhood road that runs between Bloor Street and Burnhamthorpe Road East, east of Fieldgate Drive. Work got underway this week and will continue into November. Timelines may change due to weather and other unexpected events. “Sanitary sewers are underground pipes that carry wastewater from your home to a water resource recovery facility. Wastewater is created when water goes down a drain or toilet,” project officials said in a notice to area residents and businesses. “We’ll clean the sewer pipe and place a new resin (plastic) lining inside to extend its life. ” The work is being completed by Capital Sewer Services Inc. under contract to Peel Region. m. , Monday to Friday, the region noted. During the work period, project leaders say they may need to temporarily reduce traffic to a single lane on the busy street. “If this is needed, we will place signs giving directions.

items.title: How a Mississauga bowling alley became a destination for live music and charity
items.summary: A bowling alley might not be the first place that comes to mind for a night of classic rock or new wave, but Ed Sousa has turned Mississauga’s Classic Bowl into an unlikely concert destination. Sousa, a director at the bowling centre with a background in marketing, has helped bring established Canadian and international acts to the venue, giving fans a chance to see familiar names without making the trip into downtown Toronto. The next show is Sunday, Oct. 25, when Michael Sadler, lead singer of progressive rock band Saga, performs at Classic Bowl with special guest David Barrett. It’s part of an expanding program that brings music lovers closer to the artists they enjoy, while helping Sousa promote the business and support charitable causes. What began as a fundraising idea for Ronald McDonald House Charities Canada has grown into three distinct concert series: McBowl, the annual charity music festival; Rock and Bowl, featuring intimate and interactive performances; and Pop Up Shows, which allow artists to perform in Mississauga when their touring schedules bring them through the area. For Sousa, the initiative is about much more than booking bands. It stems from a personal experience that left him determined to help families dealing with childhood illness. His nephew was diagnosed with leukemia in 1987 and died at age 17 on Halloween night in 1992. During those years, Sousa’s sister stayed at Ronald McDonald House off and on for five years. “I mean, without Ronald McDonald House, like, I don’t know how people with sick children make it,” Sousa said.

items.title: Weather alert again issued for Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: For the second night in a row, Mississauga and Brampton are under a weather alert. Environment Canada has issued a yellow frost advisory for the cities. Additionally, it covers St. Catharines, Grimsby, Niagara Falls, Welland, and Niagara Region as a whole. “Patchy frost is expected tonight, particularly for inland areas,” Environment Canada said. “Take preventative measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees, and crops. ” It’s the latest of several frost advisories issued by Environment Canada this week. Areas shaded in yellow are under a frost advisory from Environment Canada. Patchy frost is expected overnight, mainly for areas away from the lakes. Forecasters are predicting a low of 2 C. items.title: Construction begins on major upgrade to large park in Mississauga
items.summary: Construction has begun to significantly upgrade a large park in Mississauga’s east end, the city said this week. Mississauga Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca said in an update to the community that “construction is underway” at popular Garnetwood Park, where a number of amenities are being added. The “concrete forming” phase of the project, where crews build the formwork (molds into which concrete will later be poured), began earlier this month. Workers are now onto the next stage, where construction moves forward. Fonseca said earlier the City of Mississauga is adding “incredible amenities” to the 34-acre park located alongside Etobicoke Creek, near Burnhamthorpe Road East and Ponytrail Drive. The green space already features basketball nets, a leash-free zone, mobile food vendor, multi-use court, a playground, soccer field, softball diamond and a renovated spray pad, in addition to a new four-court tennis facility that opened last year. Acting on feedback from the community, the city is now adding two new paved paths to the trail system, new four-season seating/tables, a seasonal ice rink surface and pickleball courts. The upgraded spray pad was completed this past summer. Neither Fonseca nor City of Mississauga officials have provided a specific timeline for completion of the other amenities. The City of Mississauga, along with Tennis Canada and National Bank, opened the renovated Garnetwood Park Tennis Courts in June 2025. The four-court tennis facility received the makeover through National Bank’s Play Your Court program.

items.title: Brr-ing on the cold: Get your home winter-ready with these fall maintenance tips
items.summary: As winter rolls in, it can bring some risks to your property. Taking time to inspect your home and yard can help protect against weather-related damage. As Mississauga trades summer sunshine for sweater weather, falling leaves and crisp autumn days, now is the time to prepare for what comes next: winter. Before colder temperatures set in, take time to inspect and clean your property to help protect against weather-related challenges. Being proactive before temperatures drop can help prevent costly damage from colder conditions. This critical upkeep acts as a preventive measure to protect against fire damage (from heating sources), water damage (from frozen pipes) and structural damage (from wind, ice and snow buildup), while helping ensure your home and property are well maintained. Start by winterizing your home and yard. Here are a few ways to protect your property and keep it safe, warm and comfortable through the winter months. Help protect your home from winter weather by ensuring eavestroughs and downspouts are free of leaves, pine needles, sticks and other debris. Keeping them clear ensures proper drainage and helps prevent leaks and water damage. Consider disconnecting roof downspouts from pipes connected to your basement weepers, which help drain water away from your foundation. Instead, direct the runoff onto your lawn or garden using an elbow and downspout extension, ensuring water drains at least three feet away from your home’s foundation. Pruning trees and hedges before winter promotes healthy spring growth, helps prevent damage from heavy snowfall and improves the appearance of your landscape. Storing rain barrels and turning off outdoor faucets helps conserve water, prevent flooding and protect plumbing from freezing.

items.title: Want to manage an ice rink this winter in Mississauga? City opens volunteer applications for residents
items.summary: Get today's top news across Ontario for Oct. 23, including … Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9… Although weather-dependent, the natural ice rink season is expected to begin mid-December and last through March 2027. The City of Mississauga is looking for volunteers to maintain natural ice rinks in city parks between December to January, depending on the weather. If you’re interested in ice skating close to home this year, the City of Mississauga is accepting volunteer applications for its natural ice rink program. The program is community volunteer-run and provides residents with free outdoor places to skate and play hockey. According to the city, 102 volunteers participated in last year’s winter program to maintain local ice rinks across the city. Applications are being accepted until Nov. 15. To manage a rink, a minimum of three volunteers are required for daily upkeep.

In a particularly heated debate on Oct. ” “She can be very Trumpian,” Crombie told Canada’s National Observer, reflecting on her exchanges with Parrish at the debate. “I took her to task on her comments, but I never resorted to name calling,” she added. But voters have grown so dissatisfied with the candidates’ straying from policy to personal attacks that the mayoral bid is no longer a two-horse race. items.title: Three Indigenous women artists share songs and stories behind the music at Living Arts Centre
items.summary: The tour will continue in Guelph, Oakville and Toronto. (Left to right) Mimi O’Bonsawin, Celeigh Cardinal and Lacey Hill perform live during the She Carries the Song tour 2026. Three women, Indigenous singers and songwriters, are performing across Ontario, bringing their music and stories to regional venues including the Living Arts Centre in Mississauga. The trio is performing at the venue located at 4141 Living Arts Dr. Oct. m. onwards. The show, She Carries the Song, is a collaboration between Abenaki (W8banaki) singer-songwriter Mimi O’Bonsawin, Cree artist Celeigh Cardinal and Oneida/Mohawk artist Lacey Hill. The tour — which started from Ottawa and ends in Toronto — is co-ordinated by Ontario Presents, booking agencies and local performing arts centres, O’Bonsawin shared in an interview with Mississauga News. Beyond music, the performance weaves in storytelling, with artists sharing personal histories, cultural roots and the inspiration behind their songs. O’Bonsawin, who released a new record in August, said the format gives audiences a unique chance to discover three distinct styles in a single evening.
